description.value: The study evaluated a combined stop-signal alcohol-cue functional neuroimaging task in heavy drinkers to examine inhibitory control and cue-elicited craving and their relationship with alcohol-use severity.

Because all subjects were right-handed, they were instructed to respond to left-facing arrows by pressing a button with their index finger and to right-facing arrows by pressing a button with their middle finger.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to respond to left-facing arrows with the index finger and to right-facing arrows with the middle finger, and to inhibit the response when an auditory stop tone was presented. They received detailed instructions before scanning and practiced the task before acquisition.

spans.text: Before entering the scanner, participants were presented with detailed instructions for the SSACT and were then given an opportunity to practice the task and ask the research assistant for assistance or clarification if necessary.

stimuli.value: Alcoholic beverage pictures or nonalcoholic control beverage pictures such as juice or Gatorade were presented above a white circle. A left- or right-facing arrow appeared in the circle 500 ms later, and on stop trials an auditory beep was presented up to 700 ms after the arrow.

spans.text: The go cue was either a left-facing or a right-facing arrow, which appeared immediately after the alcohol or control picture was presented ( Figure 1 ).
